production.note: US model years: KBB lists the 488 GTB for 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019. TFLcar's US review is of the '2016 Ferrari 488 GTB' (tflcar-488). Evo titles the car '2015 - 2019' in calendar years and says 'The 488 GTB and 488 Pista gave way to the F8 Tributo in 2019' (evo-488). The 488 Spider and 488 Pista are separate models.

body.note: Two-seat mid-engined berlinetta; the open car is the separately named 488 Spider.

displacementL.note: 3,902 cc. Evo spec panel: 'V8, 3902cc, twin-turbo'; Ferrari's specification list as printed by Arrive Alive: 'Overall displacement 3902 cm3' (arrivealive-488).

transmission.note: 'Pairs a 3.9-litre, twin-turbocharged V8 with a seven-speed dual-clutch 'box.' Ferrari calls it the F1 dual-clutch gearbox ('seven-gear F1 dual-clutch gearbox', arrivealive-488). No manual was offered.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 670 cv x 0.98632 = 661 hp. Quote (ferrari.com, US pages): "It delivers 670 cv at 8,000 rpm with a specific power output of 172 cv/l, a new record for a road-going Ferrari, maximum torque of 760 Nm in seventh gear and a throttle response time of just 0.8 seconds at 2000 rpm in third gear." Ferrari's specification list as printed by Arrive Alive (arrivealive-488): "Maximum power * 492 kW (670 CV) at 8000 rpm", footnote "With 98 RON petrol". No separate SAE rating for the US was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS; US and UK publications print the same 661 (TFLcar: 'Horsepower (bhp): 661 @ 8,000 rpm'; Evo: '661bhp @ 8000rpm').

weightLb.note: 1,475 kg x 2.20462 = 3,252 lb (Evo prints it as plain "Weight"; TFLcar calls it curb weight). Coupe with the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox (the only transmission). Quote (Evo specification panel for the 488 GTB): "Weight | 1475kg (455bhp/ton)". TFLcar's US review of the 2016 car prints the same figure in pounds (tflcar-488): "Curb Weight: 3,252 lbs. – weight distribution=41.5% front / 58.5% rear". Ferrari's own press specification gives only a dry weight: "Dry weight** 1370 kg", footnote "With lightweight options" (arrivealive-488). The published kerb figure is exactly 105 kg above that optioned dry weight, so it very probably also assumes the lightweight options. No US-specific figure was found. Under the guide's weight order this is step 3 (a curb weight for a car with lightweight options; here very probably Ferrari's unnamed lightweight options), adopted on 2 October 2026: no curb weight for a standard car was found, and a standard car is somewhat heavier.

discrepancies.reason: Dry vs curb. Ferrari's press specification lists only a dry weight (no fluids), footnoted 'With lightweight options'; the magazines print the kerb weight.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the published kerb figure under weight step 3 (an optioned car's curb weight), since no standard-car curb weight was found and a curb weight ranks above a dry weight.
